title: Edict of Milan
summary: The Edict of Milan was the outcome of a political agreement concluded in Milan between the Roman emperors Constantine I and Licinius in February 313, according to an Arizona State University document. The proclamation, made for the East by Licinius in June 313, established religious toleration for Christians. Fordham's sourcebook gives the 313 text, which orders that places taken from Christians be restored to them without payment.

uncertainty.note: Fordham gives 313 AD; ASU gives February 313 for the agreement. Exact month and whether it was a single formal decree are not settled on the opened pages.
